text:
Alex C: Quick signal — eu-west GPU pools hit ~95% sustained for the 07:30-09:00 window today. Lots of short chatty inference; tail latencies spiking. 
Tanvi R: saw that too. Request rates up from a couple of customers + a spike in background eval jobs.
Jonah P: Do we have head-of-line blocking evidence? i.e. large batches stalling small requests?
Keiko S: HL blocking visible. Logs: `worker-42 queue wait 3.2s for big-batch` repeated. Also KV cache reuse falls when we mix long + short seqs.
Alex C: Thinking we need a hybrid scheduler: per-route soft queues for predictable fairness, but priority lanes for small low-latency routes. Dynamic admission control to shift capacity.
Kevin L: What's the intended policy for aging? we can't starve cheap background jobs forever.
Tanvi R: Proposal sketch: 
- Per-route windowed queues to keep per-customer budgets (protect multi-tenant fairness)
- A small reserved latency-priority lane for <=512 token requests (fast-path)
- Token-bucket shaping per-pool to limit burst from eval pipelines
- Aging: increase priority weight by X% per 5s wait (bounded).
Jonah P: That sounds reasonable. Concern: prefix/KV cache locality — separating routes might reduce reuse and raise token cost. We should prefer grouping by model+prefixhash where possible.
Alex C: Agreed. Hybrid should be model-aware: co-locate same model/prefix into same sub-queue when feasible so KV hits stay high.
Keiko S: Also need fallbacks across regions. If eu-west pool saturated, smart routing -> eu-central warm pool for non-SLA customers. But that affects data locality + egress cost.
Kevin L: Can we simulate cost impact quickly? rough numbers: cross-region adds ~0.5ms network + 12% egress cost for that traffic.
Tanvi R: For admission control we can use an instantaneous utility function: U = alpha*(latency_sla_score) - beta*(cost_per_token) + gamma*(fairness_penalty). Tune alpha/beta/gamma per customer tier.
Jonah P: Implementation sketch: admission controller watches per-pool fill, CPU/GPU utilization, KV hit rate. For each new request compute accept/drop/routeDecision.
Keiko S: Pseudocode we can test in sim harness: 
```
if pool.util > 0.9 and req.len > 2048: 
  drop_or_defer(req)
elif pool.util > 0.95 and req.route not in high_priority: 
  if token_bucket.consume(1) == false: defer
else accept
```
We should add metrics emitted: queue_depth_by_route, kv_hit_by_model, wait_time_histogram, admission_decisions.
Alex C: Who can own a PoC sim? need to exercise: mixed workloads (chatty small reqs, long generation, bulk evals) + topology (2 regions, warm pool).
Tanvi R: I can spin up a sim using existing loadgen, supplement with model-aware routing heuristics. Will need 1 day to prototype.
Kevin L: I'll build a cost model overlay and run a few scenarios.
Jonah P: I'll draft a design doc with specific queue semantics (max per-route backlog, priority lane size, aging schedule) and a compatibility checklist for KV locality.
Keiko S: Add a test for failure modes: GPU OOM during backlog, network partition between control-plane and pool, and stale KV leading to misses.
Alex C: Nice. Action items: 
- Tanvi: sim PoC (due EOD Fri)
- Kevin: cost delta sims (due Mon)
- Jonah: design doc + config schema (draft Tue)
- Keiko: failure-mode tests (start after PoC)
I'll post summary to #eng-platform after we have PoC numbers. :thumbsup:
